components.name: appbar
components.title: app bar
components.line: a one-row bar docked to the top
components.contract: props brand, title, style; slot: the right side; reads app.user, app.env
components.source:
<!-- k-appbar · Contract: props brand, title, style; slot: the right side; reads app.user, app.env · Actions: none · Keys: none · Requires: k-badge -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col id="app" width="1fr" height="1fr">
      <!-- COPY: the app bar is one row docked to the top of its parent, so
           the content below keeps all the remaining space. What you write
           inside the use goes on the right. Put at most one top-docked bar
           in a container. A page title from data is the class markup:
           <row class="k-appbar"> with its own k-appbar-* texts. -->
      <use template="k-appbar" brand="◆ orbit" title="Deployments">
        <text class="k-appbar-meta">{app.user}</text>
        <text class="k-badge ok">{app.env}</text>
      </use>
      <col width="1fr" height="1fr" pad="1">
        <text class="k-muted">The page content goes here.</text>
      </col>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-appbar: a one-row bar docked to the top. Props: brand, title, style.
     Slot: the right side (meta text, badges). -->
<template id="k-appbar" props="brand title style">
  <row class="k-appbar" style="{$style}">
    <text class="k-appbar-brand">{$brand}</text>
    <text class="k-appbar-title">{$title}</text>
    <spacer/>
    <slot/>
  </row>
</template>

components.name: statusbar
components.title: status bar
components.line: a one-row bar docked to the bottom, with filled segments
components.contract: reads status.mode, status.file, status.synced, status.position
components.source:
<!-- k-statusbar · Contract: reads status.mode, status.file, status.synced, status.position · Actions: none · Keys: none · Requires: k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col id="app" width="1fr" height="1fr">
      <col width="1fr" height="1fr" pad="1">
        <text class="k-muted">The page content goes here.</text>
      </col>
      <!-- COPY: the status bar is a one-row `row` with class `k-statusbar`,
           docked to the bottom of its parent. Left segments first, a
           `spacer`, then right segments. `k-statusbar-seg` is a filled chip
           (modifiers: ok, warn, danger); `k-statusbar-text` and
           `k-statusbar-muted` are plain. Only one bottom-docked bar per
           container (L005): put the key hints above it, not docked. -->
      <row class="k-statusbar">
        <text class="k-statusbar-seg">{status.mode}</text>
        <text class="k-statusbar-text">{status.file}</text>
        <spacer/>
        <text class="k-statusbar-seg ok" if="status.synced">synced</text>
        <text class="k-statusbar-seg warn" if="!status.synced">unsynced</text>
        <text class="k-statusbar-muted">{status.position}</text>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: breadcrumb
components.title: breadcrumb
components.line: the current path, down to the last crumb on a narrow terminal
components.contract: with="PATH as b", where PATH is an array of {id, label, last}; reads where; the host trims the array on breadcrumb_up
components.source:
<!-- k-breadcrumb · Contract: with="PATH as b", where PATH is an array of {id, label, last}; reads where; the host trims the array on breadcrumb_up · Actions: breadcrumb_up · Keys: backspace (up) · Requires: k-hints, k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="backspace" action="breadcrumb_up" label="up"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1">
      <!-- USE: the k-breadcrumb template over an array of {id, label, last}.
           Each crumb is a label (marked `current` when it is the last) and a
           separator. The host builds the array from the current path and
           trims it on `breadcrumb_up`. The crumbs are display only (a
           repeated row holds nothing focusable): navigate with a keymap
           row. -->
      <use template="k-breadcrumb" with="crumbs as b"/>
      <text class="k-muted" pad="1">You are in {where}.</text>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-breadcrumb: the current path. Props: style. with="PATH as b", where
     PATH is an array of {id, label, last}. -->
<template id="k-breadcrumb" props="style">
  <row class="k-breadcrumb" each="b as crumb" key="crumb.id" style="{$style}">
    <text class="k-breadcrumb-item" class:current="crumb.last">{crumb.label}</text>
    <text class="k-breadcrumb-sep" if="!crumb.last">›</text>
  </row>
</template>

components.name: tabs
components.title: tabs
components.line: a tab strip bound to a path
components.contract: reads and writes view (the active tab's id); reads tabs.overview, tabs.activity, tabs.settings, tabs.count
components.actions: none (the keymap uses the built-ins move-next, move-prev, switch-to)
components.source:
<!-- k-tabs · Contract: reads and writes view (the active tab's id); reads tabs.overview, tabs.activity, tabs.settings, tabs.count · Actions: none (the keymap uses the built-ins move-next, move-prev, switch-to) · Keys: ] and [ move, 1 to 3 switch · Requires: k-card, k-hints -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="]" action="move-next" to="#nav" keycap="]/[" label="tab"/>
    <bind keys="[" action="move-prev" to="#nav"/>
    <bind keys="1" action="switch-to" to="#overview"/>
    <bind keys="2" action="switch-to" to="#activity"/>
    <bind keys="3" action="switch-to" to="#settings"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0">
      <!-- COPY: tabs are a `tabs` with class `k-tabs` bound to a path that
           holds the active tab's id (the host or `switch-to` writes it).
           Write `focusable` on it: whether a tab strip takes focus is then
           your choice, not a default. Each `tab` needs an `id` (yours, not
           a kit part: it is the value of the bound path) and a `label`;
           `short` is the label used when the strip does not fit. The
           generated labels are styled by the class (`.k-tabs > .tab-label`).
           Only the active tab's content is laid out. `mark` is the glyph
           before the active label. -->
      <tabs id="nav" class="k-tabs" bind="view" mark="▸" focusable="true">
        <tab id="overview" label="1 overview" short="1 ovr">
          <box class="k-card" title="Overview">
            <text class="k-card-text">{tabs.overview}</text>
          </box>
        </tab>
        <tab id="activity" label="2 activity ({tabs.count})" short="2 act">
          <box class="k-card" title="Activity">
            <text class="k-card-text">{tabs.activity}</text>
          </box>
        </tab>
        <tab id="settings" label="3 settings" short="3 set">
          <box class="k-card" title="Settings">
            <text class="k-card-text">{tabs.settings}</text>
          </box>
        </tab>
      </tabs>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: split
components.title: split pane
components.line: a list beside a detail card, stacked on a narrow terminal
components.contract: reads items[] {id, title, age}, detail.{title, status, open, age, summary, owner} (the host keeps detail with a Derive over items and the cursor); reads and writes cur (the cursor row's id)
components.source:
<!-- k-split · Contract: reads items[] {id, title, age}, detail.{title, status, open, age, summary, owner} (the host keeps detail with a Derive over items and the cursor); reads and writes cur (the cursor row's id) · Actions: menu_select · Keys: j and k move · Requires: k-menu, k-card, k-badge, k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <keymap when="#items">
    <bind keys="j" action="move-next"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="move-prev"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#items">
    <!-- COPY: master / detail is a `row` with class `k-split`: a list on the
         left (`k-split-master`, 34% wide, 24 to 40 columns) and a card on
         the right (`k-split-detail`, the rest). The list `bind` is the
         selected id; the host keeps `detail` (a Derive over `items` and the
         cursor) so the right side follows the cursor with no handler.
         The detail card shows the badge for the status through class:NAME
         guards. -->
    <row class="k-split">
      <list id="items" class="k-menu k-split-master" each="items as it" key="it.id" bind="cur" title="Incidents" on:select="menu_select">
        <item>
          <row class="k-menu-row">
            <text class="k-menu-label">{it.title}</text>
            <text class="k-menu-key">{it.age}</text>
          </row>
        </item>
      </list>
      <box class="k-card k-split-detail" title="{detail.title}">
        <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
          <text class="k-badge" class:danger="detail.open" class:ok="!detail.open">{detail.status}</text>
          <text class="k-muted">{detail.age} ago</text>
        </row>
        <text class="k-card-text" wrap="wrap">{detail.summary}</text>
        <text class="k-card-muted">owner: {detail.owner}</text>
      </box>
    </row>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: hints
components.title: key hints
components.line: the keymap’s labeled rows as a row of hints
components.contract: reads nothing from the store; shows the keymap rows that have a label
components.actions: none of its own (the demo names item_new, item_open, item_next, item_prev, item_search)
components.source:
<!-- k-hints · Contract: reads nothing from the store; shows the keymap rows that have a label · Actions: none of its own (the demo names item_new, item_open, item_next, item_prev, item_search) · Keys: whatever the keymap binds · Requires: k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <!-- COPY: every keymap row with a `label` becomes a hint. `keycap` is the
       text shown instead of the key (use it for "j/k" or "^S"). A row
       without a label is bound but not shown. -->
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="n" action="item_new" label="new"/>
    <bind keys="enter" action="item_open" label="open"/>
    <bind keys="j" action="item_next" keycap="j/k" label="move"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="item_prev"/>
    <bind keys="/" action="item_search" label="search"/>
    <bind keys="q" action="quit" label="quit"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col id="app" width="1fr" height="1fr">
      <col width="1fr" height="1fr" pad="1">
        <text class="k-muted">The page content goes here.</text>
      </col>
      <!-- COPY: `<hints/>` with class `k-hints`: one row, the key in the
           accent color (`.hint-key`), the label muted (`.hint-label`; the
           class styles both). Hints that do not fit are dropped from the
           right. `scope="active"` (the default) shows only the keys that
           would fire right now. -->
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: card
components.title: card
components.line: a bordered panel with a title that takes the focus color while it holds focus
components.contract: props title, style; slot: the body; reads card.heading, card.text
components.source:
<!-- k-card · Contract: props title, style; slot: the body; reads card.heading, card.text · Actions: card_open, card_dismiss (the demo's buttons) · Keys: tab, enter · Requires: k-btn, k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#card__open">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">card / panel</text>
      <!-- COPY: a card is a titled box; what you write inside the use is its
           body, with your own paths, ids and actions. The border turns to
           the focus color while anything inside holds focus. It wraps its
           content; style="height: 10" (or 1fr) fixes it. A title from data
           is the class markup: <box class="k-card" title="{PATH}">. -->
      <use template="k-card" title="Deploy">
        <text class="k-card-title">{card.heading}</text>
        <text class="k-card-muted">{card.text}</text>
        <row class="k-card-actions">
          <button id="card__open" class="k-btn primary" label="Open" on:click="card_open"/>
          <button id="card__dismiss" class="k-btn ghost" label="Dismiss" on:click="card_dismiss"/>
        </row>
      </use>
      <!-- COPY: side-by-side cards share the row; each takes `1fr`. -->
      <row width="1fr" height="auto" gap="1">
        <use template="k-card" title="Left">
          <text class="k-card-text">First card</text>
        </use>
        <use template="k-card" title="Right">
          <text class="k-card-text">Second card</text>
        </use>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-card: a titled panel. Props: title, style. Slot: the body. A card
     whose title comes from data is the class markup,
     <box class="k-card" title="{PATH}">. -->
<template id="k-card" props="title style">
  <box class="k-card" title="{$title}" style="{$style}">
    <slot/>
  </box>
</template>

components.name: kv
components.title: key / value
components.line: a muted label and a value on one row, for a card of facts
components.contract: props label, style; with="PATH as v" reads v, the value
components.source:
<!-- k-kv · Contract: props label, style; with="PATH as v" reads v, the value · Actions: none · Keys: none · Requires: k-card, k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">key / value</text>
      <!-- COPY: one row per field, in a card: the label is literal, the
           value is a path. The label column is 8 wide; a sheet rule
           (.k-kv-label { width: 10; }) widens it for every row. -->
      <use template="k-card" title="Service">
        <use template="k-kv" label="Name" with="svc.name as v"/>
        <use template="k-kv" label="Owner" with="svc.owner as v"/>
        <use template="k-kv" label="Region" with="svc.region as v"/>
        <use template="k-kv" label="Version" with="svc.version as v"/>
      </use>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-kv: one key / value row, in a card. Props: label, style.
     with="PATH as v": the value. -->
<template id="k-kv" props="label style">
  <row class="k-kv" style="{$style}">
    <text class="k-kv-label">{$label}</text>
    <text class="k-kv-value">{v}</text>
  </row>
</template>

components.name: alert
components.title: alert
components.line: a callout with an icon, in four status colors
components.contract: props title, icon, text (each optional); slot: more body, after the text; reads build.retry
components.source:
<!-- k-alert · Contract: props title, icon, text (each optional); slot: more body, after the text; reads build.retry · Actions: none · Keys: none · Requires: k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">alert / callout</text>
      <!-- USE: one <use> of the k-alert template per alert, with its
           variant as the use's class (info, ok, warn, danger) and its text
           as props (title, icon, text; each optional). The title is the box
           title; the text wraps; the variant colors the frame and the icon.
           What you write inside the <use> (the last alert) is more body,
           after the text, with the paths of this document. -->
      <use template="k-alert" class="info" title="Heads up" icon="i" text="Deploys are paused until 09:00 UTC."/>
      <use template="k-alert" class="ok" title="Saved" icon="✓" text="Your changes are live in every region."/>
      <use template="k-alert" class="warn" title="Quota" icon="!" text="You have used 92% of this month's build minutes."/>
      <use template="k-alert" class="danger" title="Build failed" icon="✗" text="Step 3 exited with code 1: tests failed in pkg/router.">
        <text>{build.retry}</text>
      </use>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-alert: a callout. Props: title, icon, text, style. Slot: more body,
     after the text (a dynamic line, a button). Variant: info, ok, warn,
     danger. -->
<template id="k-alert" props="title icon text style">
  <box class="k-alert" title="{$title}" style="{$style}">
    <row class="k-alert-row">
      <text class="k-alert-icon">{$icon}</text>
      <col class="k-alert-body">
        <text class="k-alert-text">{$text}</text>
        <slot/>
      </col>
    </row>
  </box>
</template>

components.name: badge
components.title: badge
components.line: a short status label, with a modifier for its color
components.contract: reads build.number, build.status, build.ok
components.source:
<!-- k-badge · Contract: reads build.number, build.status, build.ok · Actions: none · Keys: none · Requires: k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <!-- The kit: its sheets, its overlay keys and its templates. Your own
       sheet, if any, comes after it. -->
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">badge</text>
      <!-- COPY: a badge is one text with two classes: `k-badge` and a
           modifier. Modifiers: accent, ok, warn, danger, info (none =
           neutral). The label is literal text or a {path}. -->
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
        <text class="k-badge">draft</text>
        <text class="k-badge accent">new</text>
        <text class="k-badge ok">passing</text>
      </row>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
        <text class="k-badge warn">flaky</text>
        <text class="k-badge danger">failed</text>
        <text class="k-badge info">{build.number}</text>
      </row>
      <!-- COPY: choose the modifier from data with class:NAME guards on the
           same node (the guards are paths the host keeps true or false). -->
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
        <text class="k-badge" class:ok="build.ok" class:danger="!build.ok">{build.status}</text>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: stat
components.title: stat
components.line: a KPI card with a change and a sparkline
components.contract: props title, min, max (the sparkline range); with="PATH as s" reads s.value, s.delta, s.hist[] (numbers), and the flags s.good and s.bad
components.source:
<!-- k-stat · Contract: props title, min, max (the sparkline range); with="PATH as s" reads s.value, s.delta, s.hist[] (numbers), and the flags s.good and s.bad · Actions: none · Keys: none · Requires: k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">stat / KPI card</text>
      <!-- USE: the k-stat template: the `title` prop as the box title, the
           value in bold, and a row with the change and a sparkline of s.hist. The
           flags s.good and s.bad turn the change green or red (whether a
           rise is good depends on the metric, so the host decides). `min`
           and `max` fix the sparkline's range (without them it comes from
           the values). Put
           stats in a row; each takes `1fr` of the width. -->
      <row width="1fr" height="auto" gap="1">
        <use template="k-stat" title="Requests" with="stats.req as s"/>
        <use template="k-stat" title="Errors" min="0" with="stats.err as s"/>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-stat: a KPI card. Props: title, min, max (the sparkline's range),
     style. with="PATH as s": s.value, s.delta, s.hist (numbers); flags
     s.good and s.bad color the change. -->
<template id="k-stat" props="title min max style">
  <box class="k-stat" title="{$title}" style="{$style}">
    <text class="k-stat-value">{s.value}</text>
    <row class="k-stat-row">
      <text class="k-stat-delta" class:good="s.good" class:bad="s.bad">{s.delta}</text>
      <sparkline class="k-stat-spark" bind="s.hist" min="{$min}" max="{$max}"/>
    </row>
  </box>
</template>

components.name: meter
components.title: labeled progress
components.line: a label, a value and a bar in eighths
components.contract: prop label; with="PATH as m" reads m.text, m.pct (0 to 100), and the flags m.ok, m.warn and m.danger
components.source:
<!-- k-meter · Contract: prop label; with="PATH as m" reads m.text, m.pct (0 to 100), and the flags m.ok, m.warn and m.danger · Actions: none · Keys: none · Requires: k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">labeled progress</text>
      <!-- USE: the k-meter template: a head row (the label on the left, the
           value text on the right) over a progress bar of m.pct, a number
           from 0 to 100. Color the bar with a variant on the use (ok, warn,
           danger), or from data with the flags m.ok, m.warn and m.danger.
           The host updates the number (and the text) as the work
           advances. -->
      <use template="k-meter" label="Uploading artifact.tar" with="meters.upload as m"/>
      <use template="k-meter" label="Disk" with="meters.disk as m"/>
      <use template="k-meter" class="ok" label="Tests" with="meters.tests as m"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-meter: a labeled progress bar. Props: label, style. with="PATH as m":
     m.text, m.pct (0 to 100); flags m.ok, m.warn, m.danger. Variant: ok,
     warn, danger. -->
<template id="k-meter" props="label style">
  <col class="k-meter" style="{$style}">
    <row class="k-meter-head">
      <text class="k-meter-label">{$label}</text>
      <spacer/>
      <text class="k-meter-value">{m.text}</text>
    </row>
    <progress class="k-meter-bar" class:ok="m.ok" class:warn="m.warn" class:danger="m.danger" bind="m.pct"/>
  </col>
</template>

components.name: empty
components.title: empty state
components.line: an icon, a title, a line of help and a call to action, centered
components.contract: props icon, title, text (icon and text optional); slot: the call to action, your button and your action
components.source:
<!-- k-empty · Contract: props icon, title, text (icon and text optional); slot: the call to action, your button and your action · Actions: deploy_create (the demo's button) · Keys: enter on the button · Requires: k-btn, k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#deploy__create">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">empty state</text>
      <!-- USE: the k-empty template fills the space left and centers an
           icon, a title and one line of help, all props (the icon and the
           text are optional), then its content: the call to action. The
           button, its id and its action are yours (deploy__create fires
           deploy_create), so the use needs no id and reads no data. Show it
           with `if="!items.any"` on the <use>, next to the list it
           replaces. -->
      <use template="k-empty" icon="◌" title="No deployments yet" text="Push a commit or create one by hand.">
        <button id="deploy__create" class="k-btn primary" label="New deployment" on:click="deploy_create"/>
      </use>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-empty: an empty state, centered in the space left. Props: icon,
     title, text, style. Slot: the call to action (your button, your
     action). -->
<template id="k-empty" props="icon title text style">
  <col class="k-empty" style="{$style}">
    <text class="k-empty-icon">{$icon}</text>
    <text class="k-empty-title">{$title}</text>
    <text class="k-empty-text">{$text}</text>
    <slot/>
  </col>
</template>

components.name: log
components.title: log panel
components.line: a scrolling log that follows its end
components.contract: with="PATH as l" reads l.title and l.lines[] {n, text, debug, info, warn, err}; the host appends lines and writes the title
components.keys: j and k scroll, g top, G follow
components.source:
<!-- k-log · Contract: with="PATH as l" reads l.title and l.lines[] {n, text, debug, info, warn, err}; the host appends lines and writes the title · Actions: log_append (the host's key) · Keys: j and k scroll, g top, G follow · Requires: k-hints -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <!-- The log's scroll is log__view (the use's id, then the template's
       `view`): a keymap names it to give it keys. -->
  <keymap when="#log__view">
    <bind keys="j" action="move-next" keycap="j/k" label="scroll"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="move-prev"/>
    <bind keys="G" action="move-last" label="follow"/>
    <bind keys="g" action="move-first" label="top"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#log__view">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0">
      <!-- USE: the k-log template is a focusable scroll with
           `stick="bottom"`: it follows the end of its content as lines are
           appended, until you scroll up to read; `move-last` (or scrolling
           to the end) makes it follow again. Each line is colored by its
           flags (debug, info, warn, err): every line carries all four,
           `false` for the ones it is not. The host appends lines to the
           array and writes the title (see examples/kit-gallery). -->
      <use id="log" template="k-log" with="log as l"/>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-log: a scrolling log that follows its end. Props: style.
     with="PATH as l": l.title and l.lines, an array of {n, text, debug,
     info, warn, err}. Its scroll is U__view. -->
<template id="k-log" props="style">
  <scroll id="view" class="k-log" stick="bottom" focusable="true" title="{l.title}" style="{$style}">
    <col class="k-log-lines" each="l.lines as line" key="line.n">
      <text class="k-log-line" class:muted="line.debug" class:info="line.info" class:warn="line.warn" class:danger="line.err">{line.text}</text>
    </col>
  </scroll>
</template>

components.name: table
components.title: data table
components.line: a table with a header, right-aligned numbers and columns that hide by priority
components.contract: reads services[] {id, name, state, ok, region, rps, p95} and count; reads and writes cur (the cursor row's id)
components.keys: j and k move, enter opens
components.source: {s.name}{s.state}{s.region}{s.rps}{s.p95}

components.name: menu
components.title: menu
components.line: a navigation list with icons, shortcuts and optional check marks
components.contract: reads menu.items[] {id, icon, label, key}, menu.checked[]; reads and writes menu.cur (the cursor row's id)
components.keys: j and k move, space marks, enter opens
components.source:
<!-- k-menu · Contract: reads menu.items[] {id, icon, label, key}, menu.checked[]; reads and writes menu.cur (the cursor row's id) · Actions: menu_select, menu_open · Keys: j and k move, space marks, enter opens · Requires: k-hints, k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <keymap when="#menu">
    <bind keys="j" action="move-next"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="move-prev"/>
    <bind keys="space" action="check-toggle" label="mark"/>
    <bind keys="enter" action="menu_open" label="open"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#menu">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">menu / nav list</text>
      <!-- COPY: a menu is a `list` with class `k-menu`; each item is one
           `k-menu-row` (icon, label, shortcut). `bind` holds the cursor
           row's key; `checked` + `mark` add multi-select marks (space
           toggles it through the `check-toggle` built-in). The cursor row is
           bold on a quiet fill while another widget has focus, and a solid
           accent bar while the menu has it. Enter is not implicit in a
           list: bind it to the action that opens the row, as above. -->
      <list id="menu" class="k-menu" each="menu.items as it" key="it.id" bind="menu.cur" checked="menu.checked" mark="✓" title="Go to" on:select="menu_select">
        <item>
          <row class="k-menu-row">
            <text class="k-menu-icon">{it.icon}</text>
            <text class="k-menu-label">{it.label}</text>
            <text class="k-menu-key">{it.key}</text>
          </row>
        </item>
      </list>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: button
components.title: button
components.line: `primary`, `secondary`, `danger` and `ghost`, inverted when focused
components.contract: reads last
components.keys: tab and shift+tab move focus, enter or space presses, q quits
components.source:
<!-- k-btn · Contract: reads last · Actions: button_save, button_cancel, button_delete, button_skip · Keys: tab and shift+tab move focus, enter or space presses, q quits · Requires: k-title, k-subtitle, k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="ctrl+c,q" action="quit"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#buttons__primary">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">button</text>
      <text class="k-subtitle">tab / shift+tab moves focus; enter or space presses</text>
      <!-- COPY: a button is `k-btn` plus a modifier: primary, secondary,
           danger, ghost. `on:click` names the action (component_verb); the
           host implements it. The focused button is drawn inverted, bold and
           underlined (see `.k-btn:focus`). -->
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="buttons__primary" class="k-btn primary" label="Save" on:click="button_save"/>
        <button id="buttons__secondary" class="k-btn secondary" label="Cancel" on:click="button_cancel"/>
      </row>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="buttons__danger" class="k-btn danger" label="Delete" on:click="button_delete"/>
        <button id="buttons__ghost" class="k-btn ghost" label="Skip" on:click="button_skip"/>
        <button id="buttons__off" class="k-btn secondary" label="Locked" disabled="true"/>
      </row>
      <text class="k-muted">last action: {last}</text>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: field
components.title: form field
components.line: a label, an input, help text and an error line, with invalid styling
components.contract: props label, placeholder, help; with="forms.FORM.FIELD as f" reads f.error ("" when fine; the host writes it), and reads and writes f.value; the host also writes forms.FORM.valid, which the markup does not read
components.keys: ctrl+s saves, enter in an input submits
components.source:
<!-- k-field · Contract: props label, placeholder, help; with="forms.FORM.FIELD as f" reads f.error ("" when fine; the host writes it), and reads and writes f.value; the host also writes forms.FORM.valid, which the markup does not read · Actions: form_validate, form_submit · Keys: ctrl+s saves, enter in an input submits · Requires: k-btn, k-hints, k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="ctrl+s" action="form_submit" keycap="^S" label="save"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#profile__name__input">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">form field</text>
      <!-- USE: one k-field per field: a label, an input with its own border
           (so `:focus` can change its color), help text, and an error line.
           The use's id is FORM__FIELD, so the input is FORM__FIELD__input:
           here profile__name__input and profile__email__input, over
           forms.profile.name and forms.profile.email. The host writes the
           error ("" when fine): `invalid` turns the label and the border
           red, and the error line takes the help line's place. -->
      <use id="profile__name" template="k-field" label="Name" placeholder="your name" help="Shown on your profile." with="forms.profile.name as f"/>
      <use id="profile__email" template="k-field" label="Email" placeholder="you@example.com" help="We never share it." with="forms.profile.email as f"/>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="profile__save" class="k-btn primary" label="Save" on:click="form_submit"/>
        <hints class="k-hints"/>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-field: a form field. Props: label, placeholder, help, style.
     with="forms.FORM.FIELD as f": f.value (the input writes it), f.error
     ("" when fine). Use it as <use id="FORM__FIELD" …/>: the input is
     FORM__FIELD__input, and fires form_validate and form_submit. -->
<template id="k-field" props="label placeholder help style">
  <col class="k-field" style="{$style}">
    <text class="k-field-label" class:invalid="f.error">{$label}</text>
    <input id="input" class="k-field-input" class:invalid="f.error" bind="f.value" placeholder="{$placeholder}" on:change="form_validate" on:submit="form_submit"/>
    <text class="k-field-help" if="!f.error">{$help}</text>
    <text class="k-field-error" if="f.error">{f.error}</text>
  </col>
</template>

components.name: confirm
components.title: confirm dialog
components.line: a modal that puts the cursor on the safe button
components.contract: with="PATH as d" reads d.open, d.title, d.body, d.no and d.yes (the button labels) and the flag d.danger; slot: more body under d.body; the host writes d.open, and here confirm.result
components.keys: y confirms, n and esc cancel
components.source:
<!-- k-confirm · Contract: with="PATH as d" reads d.open, d.title, d.body, d.no and d.yes (the button labels) and the flag d.danger; slot: more body under d.body; the host writes d.open, and here confirm.result · Actions: dialog_open, dialog_confirm, dialog_cancel · Keys: y confirms, n and esc cancel · Requires: k-btn, k-title, k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#confirm__open">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">confirm dialog</text>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="confirm__open" class="k-btn danger" label="Delete project" on:click="dialog_open"/>
      </row>
      <text class="k-muted">result: {confirm.result}</text>
    </col>
    <!-- USE: the k-confirm template, as the LAST child of the screen (it is
         a modal, L004). The use's id is the instance: its parts are
         confirm__dialog, confirm__no and confirm__yes, and a host routes
         dialog_confirm and dialog_cancel by the part of the event's source
         before the last "__". `class="danger"` makes a destructive dialog
         (or set the flag d.danger from data). The cursor starts on the SAFE
         button, so a stray enter cancels; esc cancels too, and y / n work
         (the kit's <keymap when=".k-dialog">). The dialog takes the size
         of its content: as wide as the title, the text or the action row,
         up to 60 columns (and the screen), where the text wraps, and as
         tall as its content. Keep the labels short: the action row must fit
         a 40-column terminal. -->
    <use id="confirm" template="k-confirm" class="danger" with="confirm as d">
      <text class="k-muted">{confirm.detail}</text>
    </use>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-confirm: a confirm dialog that puts the cursor on the safe button,
     sized by its content (up to 60 columns, where the text wraps).
     Props: style. with="PATH as d": d.open, d.title, d.body, d.no and d.yes
     (the button labels, which name the choices; the host writes them on
     every open); flag d.danger. Slot: more body under d.body (a list, a
     checkbox); its paths are written in full, d does not exist there.
     Variant: danger. Fires dialog_confirm and dialog_cancel (esc too, and y
     and n while it is open), from U__yes, U__no or U__dialog. -->
<template id="k-confirm" props="style">
  <modal id="dialog" class="k-dialog" class:danger="d.danger" open="d.open" title="{d.title}" focus="#no" on:escape="dialog_cancel" style="{$style}">
    <text class="k-dialog-text">{d.body}</text>
    <slot/>
    <row class="k-dialog-actions">
      <spacer/>
      <button id="no" class="k-btn secondary" label="{d.no}" on:click="dialog_cancel"/>
      <button id="yes" class="k-btn primary" label="{d.yes}" on:click="dialog_confirm"/>
    </row>
  </modal>
</template>

components.name: help
components.title: help overlay
components.line: a modal that lists every labeled key
components.contract: prop title; with="PATH as h" reads h.open; lists every keymap row that has a label
components.actions: help_open, help_close (the demo also names item_new, item_delete, item_next, item_prev, item_save)
components.source:
<!-- k-help · Contract: prop title; with="PATH as h" reads h.open; lists every keymap row that has a label · Actions: help_open, help_close (the demo also names item_new, item_delete, item_next, item_prev, item_save) · Keys: ? opens, q and ? close · Requires: k-hints, k-title, k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <!-- The kit comes first, with its overlay keys: q and ? close the help
       (<keymap when=".k-help">) before they reach the global rows below,
       since the first matching row in document order wins. -->
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <!-- The help overlay shows its own "? close help" line, then every
       keymap row that has a `label`: these. (The kit's overlay keys have no
       label, so no <hints> lists them.) Give rows a `keycap` to show "j/k"
       or "^S" instead of the raw key. -->
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="?" action="help_open" label="help"/>
    <bind keys="n" action="item_new" label="new item"/>
    <bind keys="d" action="item_delete" label="delete item"/>
    <bind keys="j" action="item_next" keycap="j/k" label="move"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="item_prev"/>
    <bind keys="ctrl+s" action="item_save" keycap="^S" label="save"/>
    <bind keys="q" action="quit" label="quit"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">help overlay</text>
      <text class="k-muted">press ? for the keys</text>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
    <!-- USE: the k-help template, as the last child of the screen: a modal
         that holds `<hints scope="all">`, every labeled row, not only the
         ones that would fire right now. It is 56 columns wide and as tall
         as its content. -->
    <use id="help" template="k-help" title="Keys" with="help as h"/>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-help: every labeled key, under its own "? close help" line, in a
     scroll (U__keys) for a long keymap. Props: title, style.
     with="PATH as h": h.open. -->
<template id="k-help" props="title style">
  <modal id="dialog" class="k-help" open="h.open" title="{$title}" on:escape="help_close" style="{$style}">
    <row class="k-help-close">
      <text class="k-help-key">?</text>
      <text class="k-help-label">close help</text>
    </row>
    <scroll id="keys" class="k-help-scroll" focusable="true">
      <hints class="k-hints k-help-keys" scope="all"/>
    </scroll>
  </modal>
</template>

components.name: palette
components.title: command palette
components.line: a modal with an input over a filtered list
components.contract: props title, placeholder; with="PATH as p, FOUND as f" reads p.last, reads and writes p.open, p.query and p.cur, and reads f.any and f.items[] {id, label, hint} (the host keeps FOUND with a Derive over p.query and the commands)
components.actions: palette_open, palette_run, palette_close, palette_query (fires as the query changes; a Go host that filters with Derive needs no work in it, a TypeScript parent recomputes FOUND there)
components.keys: ctrl+k opens, up and down (or ctrl+p and ctrl+n) move, enter runs, esc closes
components.source:
<!-- k-palette · Contract: props title, placeholder; with="PATH as p, FOUND as f" reads p.last, reads and writes p.open, p.query and p.cur, and reads f.any and f.items[] {id, label, hint} (the host keeps FOUND with a Derive over p.query and the commands) · Actions: palette_open, palette_run, palette_close, palette_query (fires as the query changes; a Go host that filters with Derive needs no work in it, a TypeScript parent recomputes FOUND there) · Keys: ctrl+k opens, up and down (or ctrl+p and ctrl+n) move, enter runs, esc closes · Requires: k-hints, k-title, k-muted -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <!-- The overlay's own keys come first (the first matching row in document
       order wins). While the palette is open, up / down (and ctrl+n /
       ctrl+p) move the cursor of its list although focus stays in the
       input: the input does not consume them, so they reach the keymap,
       and the built-ins act on the list named by `to`. The list is
       palette__list (the use's id, then the template's `list`), so these
       rows live in the document, not in the kit: a kit row that named it
       would fail in every document without that palette. Enter is the
       input's `on:submit`; esc is the modal's `on:escape`. -->
  <keymap when=".k-palette">
    <bind keys="down,ctrl+n" action="move-next" to="#palette__list"/>
    <bind keys="up,ctrl+p" action="move-prev" to="#palette__list"/>
  </keymap>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="ctrl+k" action="palette_open" keycap="^K" label="commands"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">command palette</text>
      <text class="k-muted">ctrl+k opens it; type, up / down, enter, esc.</text>
      <text class="k-muted">last command: {palette.last}</text>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
    <!-- USE: the k-palette template, as the last child of the screen: an
         input bound to the query over a list of the commands that match.
         The filtering is the HOST's job (no expressions in the markup): keep
         `found` with a Derive over `palette.query` and the commands, and
         pass it as the second alias. The list's `bind` is the cursor row's
         id. The palette is 60 by 16, at most the screen. -->
    <use id="palette" template="k-palette" title="Command palette" placeholder="type a command…" with="palette as p, found as f"/>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-palette: a command palette. Props: title, placeholder, style.
     with="PATH as p, FOUND as f": p.open, p.query (the input writes it),
     p.cur (the list's cursor); f.any and f.items, an array of
     {id, label, hint} that the host keeps (a Derive over p.query). Fires
     palette_query, palette_run and palette_close (esc). Its arrows move
     U__list while the input keeps focus: add the rows that name it to your
     keymap. -->
<template id="k-palette" props="title placeholder style">
  <modal id="dialog" class="k-palette" open="p.open" title="{$title}" focus="#q" on:escape="palette_close" style="{$style}">
    <input id="q" class="k-palette-input" bind="p.query" placeholder="{$placeholder}" on:change="palette_query" on:submit="palette_run"/>
    <text class="k-palette-empty" if="!f.any">No command matches “{p.query}”.</text>
    <list id="list" class="k-palette-list" each="f.items as cmd" key="cmd.id" bind="p.cur" focusable="false">
      <item>
        <row class="k-palette-row">
          <text class="k-palette-label">{cmd.label}</text>
          <text class="k-palette-hint">{cmd.hint}</text>
        </row>
      </item>
    </list>
  </modal>
</template>

components.name: toast
components.title: toast
components.line: a one-row notice that never moves the page
components.contract: with="PATH as t" reads t.show, t.text, and the flags t.is_ok, t.is_warn and t.is_danger; the host clears t.show after a few seconds
components.source:
<!-- k-toast · Contract: with="PATH as t" reads t.show, t.text, and the flags t.is_ok, t.is_warn and t.is_danger; the host clears t.show after a few seconds · Actions: toast_show, toast_dismiss · Keys: esc dismisses · Requires: k-btn, k-title -->
<tui theme="auto">
  <include src="../kit.tui"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="esc" action="toast_dismiss" label="dismiss"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#toast__show">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">toast</text>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="toast__show" class="k-btn primary" label="Save" on:click="toast_show"/>
      </row>
      <spacer/>
      <!-- USE: the k-toast template is a one-row slot that is always there,
           so the page never jumps when the toast appears; the toast inside
           shows only while t.show is true. Info is the default; the flags
           t.is_ok, t.is_warn and t.is_danger pick another level. The HOST
           clears it: set t.show back to false from an `Every` tick (see
           examples/kit-gallery/main.go). The slot is not docked, so it can
           sit above a docked status bar (only one bottom-docked bar per
           container, L005). -->
      <use template="k-toast" with="toast as t"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
components.template:
<!-- k-toast: a one-row notice that never moves the page. Props: style.
     with="PATH as t": t.show, t.text; flags t.is_ok, t.is_warn,
     t.is_danger. -->
<template id="k-toast" props="style">
  <row class="k-toast-slot" style="{$style}">
    <row class="k-toast" if="t.show" class:ok="t.is_ok" class:warn="t.is_warn" class:danger="t.is_danger">
      <text class="k-toast-text">{t.text}</text>
      <text class="k-toast-key">esc</text>
    </row>
  </row>
</template>
